title: Most Stones Removed with Same Row or Column
description:
On a 2D plane, we place `n` stones at some integer coordinate points. Each coordinate point may contain at most one stone.

A stone can be removed if it shares either the same row or the same column as another stone that has not yet been removed.

Given an array `stones` of length `n` where `stones[i] = [xi, yi]` represents the location of the `i`-th stone, return the largest possible number of stones that can be removed.
constraints: No two stones are at the same coordinate point.
hints: View two stones as connected if they share a row or a column. Within any connected component of k stones, you can always remove k - 1 stones (for instance, by repeatedly removing leaves of a spanning tree) and leave 1 stone behind.
Therefore, the maximum number of removable stones equals total stones minus the number of connected components.

Instead of connecting stones pairwise in O(n^2), connect each stone's row index x and shifted column index y + 10001 in a Disjoint Set Union (DSU) structure to achieve near-linear O(n * alpha(n)) time.

examples.explanation: All 6 stones belong to a single connected component via shared rows and columns, so 6 - 1 = 5 stones can be removed (leaving, for example, [0, 0]).
Stones [0, 0], [0, 2], [2, 0], [2, 2] form one component of size 4 (3 removable), and [1, 1] is isolated (0 removable), for a total of 3 stones removed.
There is only one stone, so it shares a row or column with no other stone and 0 stones can be removed.
